messages:
Priya K.: hey team — first day stuff. running into a weird issue on Windows 11 w/ WSL2 + Git for Windows. my dotfiles repo uses a bunch of symlinks (e.g., .ssh -> C:\Users\Priya\dotfiles\ssh). git clone replaces symlinks with regular files on checkout. any tips?

Eli (eng): Welcome Priya! For symlinks we usually keep the repo with real files and use a small bootstrap script to create symlinks during setup. On Windows you need Developer Mode or elevated perms to create symlinks. Also prefer `git config core.symlinks false` off for WSL git.

Priya K.: ah ok — i didn’t know about Developer Mode. are there trusted scripts people run? i want to keep dotfiles cross-OS.

Morgan - DevEx: Hi Priya :wave: we have a tiny helper under `~/dotfiles/bin/bootstrap-windows.sh` that checks platform and uses `mklink` on Windows and `ln -s` elsewhere. It also prompts before overwriting. feel free to fork it.

Priya K.: thanks! another thing — corporate proxy is blocking some brew/homebrew downloads and asdf plugins fail to fetch. tried setting `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` globally but installers still error.

Sasha (IT): @Priya K. — we have an authenticated proxy on some VPNs. For Homebrew you can use `git -c http.extraHeader='Proxy-Authorization: Basic <token>' clone ...` but easier: install via an offline tarball I can share. For asdf, set `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=1` is a hack but i can open a ticket to add proxy exceptions.

Priya K.: hmm prefer not to disable SSL. if i use WSL native Linux distro, will that bypass the corporate proxy?

Eli (eng): usually WSL respects Windows proxy envs but networking can differ. Another option: mirror the asdf plugins to a private repo or use `ASDF_PLUGIN_REPO=https://github.com/<org>/asdf-plugins` if you have internal mirrors.

Priya K.: good to know. quick Q: ssh-agent on Windows — any recommended setup so VS Code + WSL share keys?

Morgan - DevEx: We recommend using the Windows `ssh-agent` service and then in WSL set `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/mnt/wsl/shared-ssh-agent.sock` via the `wsl-ssh-agent` helper. There's a short doc in the onboarding repo: https://redwood-infra/repo/onboarding/win-ssh.md :thumbsup:

Priya K.: linking the doc now. last one — 1password CLI login for CI and local dev — i need to set `OP_SESSION_<account>` env var. Any non-interactive best practice?

Sasha (IT): For local dev we allow `op account add` + `op signin --raw` to generate a session token you can `export`. For CI we put the token in the vault and inject at runtime. If you want, i can enable a short-lived service token for you for setup.

Priya K.: sweet, @Sasha that’d be amazing. thanks all — i’ll try the bootstrap script and ping if anything else breaks.

DevOnboardBot: Welcome message: Priya K. joined #new-hires (automated). Check onboarding checklist: https://redwood-infra/repo/onboarding/checklist.md

Eli (eng): Also reminder — for any credential changes ping #eng-security or open a ticket. And if you want pair-setup i’m available after 2pm today.

Priya K.: thanks eli, will take you up on that :grin:
